F1.Alert Evaluator: Owns the excursion rule (threshold held for N minutes) and opens the alert.
F1.Notification Sender: SMS to the store manager with per-store routing via Twilio.

F2.Installer Mobile App: QR scan, Wi-Fi push, provisioning claim, bind gateway to fridge.
F2.Device Identity Module: Claim-to-permanent-cert exchange so the new gateway gets an identity.
F2.Provisioning Template & Hook: Allow-list check, ERP lookup of store and asset tag, assigns thing name, group and policy.
F2.Device Registry & Groups: Thing attributes for store and fridge id/asset tag plus store-group membership must exist to be assigned.

F3.Console Web App: New config-edit screen for a group; not among the listed views.
F3.Console API: Writes desired config shadow for every thing in the target group.
F3.Device Registry & Groups: Region and fridge-type grouping beyond the current store groups.
F3.Fridge Shadow Schema: The config named shadow carries interval and thresholds.
F3.Shadow Sync Client: Delta subscription and full desired fetch on reconnect covers offline gateways.
F3.Sensor Sampler: Applies the new interval and local threshold rules.
F3.Alert Evaluator: Added after reading X/Y: cloud excursion rule must read the updated per-fridge thresholds.

F4.Console Web App: Create release, watch canary, promote in deployments view.
F4.Rollout Orchestrator: Rollout rate, 2% abort threshold, per-device execution status.
F4.Device Registry & Groups: 5% canary group and fleet group to target.
F4.OTA Update Agent: Download, verify, A/B flash, rollback, report job status.

F5.Offline Buffer: Disk FIFO sized for the outage, ordered replay.
F5.Telemetry Normalizer: Dedupe by sequence and order late replayed readings.
F5.Console API: Range query over the time-series store under store RBAC.

F6.Device Registry & Groups: Deactivate thing/cert, detach policy, remove from groups.
F6.Provisioning Template & Hook: Only cloud-side Private CA integrator (§9): revoke cert; allow-list must also reject the retired serial so it cannot re-provision.
F6.Device Health Monitor: Must not mark the retired gateway offline (spurious offline alert) or audit its cert.

keyChanges: F3: added Alert Evaluator. Both sets argued the cloud excursion rule (F1) evaluates per-fridge thresholds, so a threshold change that only reached the gateway would leave alerts firing on stale values. Convinced.

X.F1/Sensor Sampler: Already samples temperature at the configured interval; the feature uses it, changes nothing.
X.F1/Routing Rules: Shared plumbing that already routes telemetry to the ingestion stream; unchanged.
X.F1/Telemetry Normalizer: Shared plumbing that already dedupes and orders; unchanged.
X.F5/Sensor Sampler: Produces readings regardless of link state; no change for history.
X.F5/Routing Rules: Replayed telemetry is ordinary telemetry on the existing route; unchanged.
X.F6/Device Identity Module: Never-reconnect must be enforced cloud-side (deactivated cert, detached policy, CRL); on-device cooperation of a retired unit cannot be relied on and its responsibility is key holding/exchange/rotation.
X.F6/Time-series Store: Existing 90-day retention already erases readings after the retention period; no per-device store rule is needed.

Y.F1/Sensor Sampler: Same as X: used, not changed.
Y.F1/Routing Rules: Same as X: shared plumbing, unchanged.
Y.F1/Telemetry Normalizer: Same as X: shared plumbing, unchanged.
Y.F2/Console API: Store and asset tag are assigned to registry attributes by the Provisioning Hook (ERP lookup there); the BFF only reads the registry as it already does.
Y.F2/Console Web App: Fleet search is an existing view; showing one more fridge is use, not change.
Y.F6/Time-series Store: Same as X: existing retention covers it.

patterns: Both X and Y link shared telemetry plumbing (Routing Rules, Telemetry Normalizer) on F1 because the feature's data flows through it, not because the feature changes it.
Both X and Y link Sensor Sampler as an upstream 'produces the data' dependency (F1; X also on F5) where the feature only uses existing sampling.
Both X and Y link Time-series Store on F6 for erasure that the existing 90-day retention already provides.
Y links Console API and Console Web App on F2 for merely displaying data the Provisioning Hook already wrote to the registry.
X links the on-device Device Identity Module on F6 for revocation handling that must be enforced cloud-side, not on a retired gateway.
Neither set missed a required component; all errors are over-linking of used-but-unchanged components.
